_comment: Ruby naming for the cdk8s libraries, in the same shape as cdk-targets.json.
Separate file because cdk8s is an independent product with its own release
cadence: pointing JSII_RUBY_TARGET_CONFIG at this one generates cdk8s
bindings without dragging aws-cdk-lib's 20k types into the picture.
cdk8s is a far smaller assembly than aws-cdk-lib (37 types, no submodules;
cdk8s-plus-27 adds 785), and its apps synthesize to YAML with no cloud
account involved — which makes it a cheap end-to-end check that this
target produces the same semantics as the TypeScript original.
CDK8s, not Cdk8s: the name is an initialism with a digit in it, which no
casing rule is going to guess. Named explicitly so the module and every
cdk8s-plus is versioned against a Kubernetes minor (27, 28, 29 ...), and
each is a separate assembly, so each gets its own gem and module rather
than one gem that silently changes what it binds to.
